provenance: American Associated Artist's, New York | | Lot Essay | | Between 1937 and 1941, Grant Wood created 19 lithographs that were published by Associated American Artists (A.A.A.) but his 1937 print, Sultry Night, is the rarest and most unique. The A.A.A, was a Depression-era enterprise that sold original prints by American artists, offering printed images of American life in large editions, at reasonable prices, via mail order and through regional stores. Following the unveiling of the oil version of Sultry Night in early 1937 — an image inspired by Wood's childhood memories of farmhands — the lithograph was created and made available through the A.A.A. catalogue. This lithograph gained notoriety for its full-frontal portrayal of a nude man and the U.S. Post Office banned A.A.A. from mailing the print because it was considered obscene. As a result, only 100 impressions were made.
